PIT

PIT-API package. Declares the API that is required to use PIT.

Author

Juergen Sieben, ConDeS GmbH

Published under MIT licence

Public Constants
Trace and log level constants

Constants are implemented as functions to allow for accesss from SQL.

LEVEL_FATAL

Log severity of fatal errors

LEVEL_SEVERE

Log severity of severe errors

LEVEL_ERROR

Log severity of "normal" errors

LEVEL_WARN

Log severity for warn messages

LEVEL_INFO

Log severity for informational messages

LEVEL_DEBUG

Log severity for debugging messages

LEVEL_ALL

Log level for verbose messages

TRACE_OFF

Trace level to switch tracing off

TRACE_MANDATORY

Trace level for important procedure calls

TRACE_OPTIONAL

Trace level for package internal procedure calls

Formatting constants

Constants are partly implemented as functions to allow for accesss from SQL.

FORMAT_ICO

Parameter value to indicate that a message has to be formatted using ICU functionality

TRACE_DETAILED

Trace level for package internal helper procedures

TYPE_INTEGER

Constant for type checks

TYPE_NUMBER

Constant for type checks

TYPE_DATE

Constant for type checks

TYPE_TIMESTAMP

Constant for type checks

TYPE_XML

Constant for type checks

check_log_level_greater_equal
function check_log_level_greater_equal(
p_log_level 
in binary_integer
)
return boolean

Method checks whether the actually valid log level is greater or equal to P_LOG_LEVEL

Allows external code to check whether PIT is in a given log level. This is useful to run logic only if it would be logged anyway.

Parameter
p_log_level
in binary_integer

Severity to check, one of the constants <LEVEL_OFF> .. LEVEL_ALL

Returns

TRUE, if the acutally valid log level is greater or equal to P_LOG_LEVEL, FALSE otherwise

Logs a message regardless of the actual log settings.

Call this procedure to emit debug messages regardless of log settings.  Use this method if you want to emit a message anyway or if you decide to emit a log message or not in code outside PIT.

Optionally, set a list of modules that will become active for this method only. Modules set her will not remain active after this method.  The context remains unchanged.

Parameters
p_message_name
in varchar2

Name of the message. Reference to package MSG

p_msg_args
in msg_args

Optional list of replacement information

p_affected_id
in varchar2

Optional id of an item a message relates to

p_affected_ids
in msg_params

Optional list of parameters a message relates to

p_error_code
in varchar2

Optional error code, usable by external applications

p_log_threshold
in number

Optional log level for the log process. Should the severity of the requested message be higher than this level, it won't get logged. If null, the message is logged if it's severity is higher than the actual log level defined.

p_log_modules
in varchar2

Optional list of module names, separated by semicolon that is used to log the message. If NULL, the list of actually set modules is used.

log_state
procedure log_state(
p_params 
msg_params,
p_severity 
in binary_integer
 default 
null
)

Log method to log the state of variables without relation to methods ENTER or LEAVE

This method is useful if you want to log the state of several variables within a method.  This way, you can report the status of variables without the requirement to create distinct messages for those. This adds flexibility and reduces administrative workload.

Parameters
p_params
msg_params

Instance of MSG_PARAMS, containing the variable names and values to log

p_severity
in binary_integer

Log level of the state message. Values get logged only if the actual log settings are lower (mor severe) or equal to P_SEVERITY.  If NULL, parameter LOG_STATE_THRESHOLD controls whether the params get logged or not

handle_validation
procedure handle_validation

Exception handler that handles validation errors, warnings and hints

Call this procedure in EXCEPTION handlers of your code.  handle_validation not only reports the error but handles it as well.  This means that if you pass any error that occurred to this procedure, the error gets logged and handled.

handle_validation includes a call to leave, so there is no need to call leave explicitly.

This method does not accept any parameters, it is desinged so that it works with the preiviously generated message such as with pit.assert... methods.  There is no way to define new messages solely for the validation process.

leave_mandatory
procedure leave_mandatory(
p_params 
in msg_params
 default 
null
)

Traces leaving a method, level trace_mandatory

Call this procedure if you leave a method.

No call to this procedure is required in exception< blocks if you called handle_exception or stop/<reraise_exception> within the exception block, as these procedures handle this call.

Attention

It's important to make sure that any possible exit point of a method first calls this procedure to make sure that the call stack is correctlymaintained.

Also, make sure that the stack level corresponds to the respective enter method to avoid call stack confusion if the trace level is set to a lower level.

Parameter
p_params
in msg_params

Instance of msg_params with a list of key-value pairs representing parameter name and -value.

long_op
procedure long_op(
p_sofar 
in number,
p_total 
in number
 default 
100,
p_target 
in varchar2
 default 
null,
p_units 
in varchar2
 default 
null,
p_op_name 
in varchar2
 default 
null
)

Sets dbms_application_info.

Use this procedure to pass information about long operations to the database.  If this task is completed, call this procedure with

p_sofar = p_total (or p_sofar = 100)

to allow for proper state cleansing.

If you call handle_exception or stop, the state will be cleaned as well.

This method will work only if tracing is enabled, as it takes the method name from the call stack and persists the actual index with the call stack.

If you plan to call it in a loop you may only pass in the required parameters, all other values are taken from the first call.

Parameters
p_sofar
in number

Percentage of the task completed (0 .. 100 or individual scale)

p_total
in number

Amount of work to be done. Defaults to 100 (percent)

p_target
in varchar2

Description of the operation. Max length is 32 byte.

p_units
in varchar2

Unit of work, eg. "rows processed" or similar. Defaults to "iterations done"

p_op_name
in varchar2

Optional indication of the task that is performed. If NULL, the package.method name is used.  Max length is 64 byte.

Asserts that <P_CONDITION> is true.

Collect mode control
start_message_collection
procedure start_message_collection

Switches PIT collection mode on

Is used to set PIT to collect mode, where all messages are collected rather than thrown or processed immediate.  This mode allows for validation methods to perfrom all internal validations prior to raising validation errors.

stop_message_collection
procedure stop_message_collection

Switches PIT collection mode off

If called, the list of raised messages is examined.

  • If at least one message of secverity C_LEVEL_FATAL is present, exception PIT_BULK_FATAL is raised.

  • If at least one message of secverity C_LEVEL_ERROR is present, exception PIT_BULK_ERROR is raised.

To process the errors, use get_message_collection to retrieve a list of all collected messages.

has_no_bulk_error
function has_no_bulk_error
return boolean

Method to check whether no error has occurred yet.

Is used to check that no exception has occured during collection mode.  This is useful to control wether further validations do make sense.

Returns

TRUE, if no error or fatal error has occured yet, FALSE otherwise

has_no_bulk_fatal
function has_no_bulk_fatal
return boolean

Method to check whether no fatal error has occurred yet.

Is used to check that no exception has occured during collection mode.  This is useful to control wether further validations do make sense.

Returns

TRUE, if no fatal error has occured yet, FALSE otherwise

assert_is_ok
function assert_is_ok(
p_error_code 
in varchar2
 default 
null,
p_error_code_list 
in char_table
 default 
null,
p_threshold 
in varchar2
 default 
LEVEL_ERROR
)
return boolean

Method to check whether an exception has occured during collection mode.

Parameters
p_error_code
in varchar2

Optional error code to group validations. If set, it is checked whether and exception occured whithin validations for the same error code. Useful if more than one validation is used for a given attribute.  If NULL and P_ERROR_CODE_LIST is also NULL, any error within the actual collection run will trigger the result.

p_error_code_list
in char_table

Optional list of error codes. If not null, it is checked whether an exception occured within one of the mentioned groups.

p_threshold
in varchar2

Flag to set the level that triggers the evaluation. Defaults to LEVEL_ERROR, meaning that only errors and fatal errors trigger the result to be not ok. If set to LEVEL_FATAL, errors do not trigger the outcome.

Returns

Flag to indicate whether a message of leve P_THRESHOLD or more severe has occured during the actual collection run. Returns TRUE, if this has happend and FALSE otherwise.

get_message_collection
function get_message_collection
return pit_message_table

Retrieves the collection of messages raised since setting PIT to collect mode.

Is used to retrieve a list of all messages raised during the collect cycle. It implicitly terminates collection mode by calling stop_message_collection if PIT is still in collection mode.

Normal usage is terminating collection mode explicity and deal with the list of messages in the exception block.

Returns

Instance of PIT_MESSAGE_TABLE, a list of message instances.

Context control
set_context
procedure set_context(
p_log_level 
in integer,
p_trace_level 
in integer,
p_trace_timing 
in boolean,
p_log_modules 
in varchar2
)

Sets the trace context for the active session. Overloaded to directly set the context components.

Call this procedure to dynamically change the debug settings to allow for dynamic debugging from within an application.

Normal usage is to specify that the active session only should be logged and/or traced. Set the options you wish and immediately these settings apply. To reset logging to the default call reset_context

Parameters
p_log_level
in integer

Requested log level

p_trace_level
in integer

Requested stack level

p_timing_on

Flag to indicate whehter timing information should be captured.

p_log_modules
in varchar2

Colon-separated list of output modules to be used.

set_context
procedure set_context(
p_context_name 
in varchar2
)

Sets the trace context for the active session. Overloaded to directly set the context by means of a named context.

Call this procedure to set the active context to a predefined context. Contexts are defined as parameters with the name pattern

CONTEXT_<Name>

and a string value according to this pattern:

[LOG_LEVEL|TRACE_LEVEL|TRACE_TIMING_FLAG (Y,N)|MODULE_LIST],
Example
CONTEXT_FULL = '70|70|Y|PIT_CONSOLE:PIT_FILE'
Parameter
p_context_name
in varchar2

Name of the context to swithc to.

set_context_value
procedure set_context_value(
p_name 
in varchar2,
p_value 
in varchar2
)

Method to set a context value eplicitly.

Is used to persist arbitrary values at the context. This allows for maintaining information such as a test flag in a cross session aware manner. Setting an attribute to NULL eliminates this attribute from the context.

Parameters
p_name
in varchar2

Name of the attribute to set

p_value
in varchar2

Value to set, VARCHAR2 up to 4000 bytes.

get_context_value
function get_context_value(
p_name 
in varchar2
)
return varchar2

Method to get a context value eplicitly.

Is used to retrieves sert values from the context. This allows for maintaining information such as a test flag in a cross session aware manner.

Parameters
p_name
in varchar2

Name of the attribute to get

Returns

Value of the attribute <P_NAME>

reset_context
procedure reset_context(
p_active_session_only 
in boolean
 default 
true
)

Resets the trace context for the active session to the default values.

If <p_active_session_only> is true, other settings remain unchanged. If false, any active context cross session is set back to default. This option is useful to clean up any unwanted debugging.

Parameter

p_active_session_only Flag to indicate whether the active session should be reset only. Defaults to TRUE.

<ARGS>, name list of the actually active modules

initialize
procedure initialize

Re-initializes PIT

Either called implicitly upon first instantiation or explicitly upon request.  Calling this method is sometimes useful after changing PIT parameters or to clean up the call stack if the level indication ran out of sync.
